soilAnalyses.conditionSummary: Soil exhibits Neutral soil pH (6. Overall nutrient status is partially deficient in key macronutrients.

nitrogen.interpretation: Insufficient for vigorous vegetative growth. Crop will show stunted growth and pale yellowing older leaves.

phosphorus.interpretation: Poor root proliferation and delayed flowering. Older leaves may develop dark green to purplish tints.

potassium.interpretation: Optimum level. Regulates stomatal opening, enzyme activation, disease resistance, and grain grain-filling.

organicCarbon.interpretation: Depleted soil organic matter. Poor moisture retention, low microbial activity, and compacted soil structure.

deficiencies.impact: Stunted plant growth, thin stems, pale yellowish older leaves.
deficiencies.correctiveAction: Apply 25% extra nitrogen in split doses; incorporate green manure or neem coated urea.

deficiencies.impact: Poor root development, purple pigmentation on leaves, delayed flowering.
deficiencies.correctiveAction: Apply Single Super Phosphate (SSP) or DAP as basal dressing placed 5cm below seed.

deficiencies.impact: Compacted soil, poor water retention and beneficial soil microbiology.
deficiencies.correctiveAction: Add 5 tonnes/acre well-decomposed Farm Yard Manure (FYM) or 2 tonnes/acre vermicompost.

soilAnalyses.phInterpretation: Neutral soil pH (6.5 - 7.5). Optimal nutrient availability for almost all crops.
soilAnalyses.organicMatterAdvice: Apply crop residue mulching, maintain minimum tillage, and add vermicompost or composted cow dung annually before monsoon.

nutrientOverview.nitrogenRequirement: Moderate to high. Requires split applications for maximum efficiency.
nutrientOverview.phosphorusRequirement: Full dose applied at sowing for deep root establishment.
nutrientOverview.potassiumRequirement: Applied basal or split to enhance stalk strength and drought resilience.
nutrientOverview.stageSpecificFocus: Focus on root establishment and uniform tillering.

fertilizerSchedule.timing: During final land preparation or sowing
fertilizerSchedule.recommendedFertilizer: DAP (50 kg) + MOP (25 kg) + Urea (20 kg) per acre
fertilizerSchedule.applicationMethod: Deep soil placement 5cm beside seed furrow
fertilizerSchedule.purpose: Provides essential phosphorus and initial nitrogen for seedling vigor.

fertilizerSchedule.recommendedFertilizer: Neem Coated Urea (45 kg per acre)
fertilizerSchedule.purpose: Stimulates vigorous tillering and leaf canopy expansion.

fertilizerSchedule.recommendedFertilizer: Neem Coated Urea (30 kg) + Zinc Sulphate (5 kg foliar or soil)
fertilizerSchedule.applicationMethod: Top dressing followed by light irrigation
fertilizerSchedule.purpose: Enhances flowering percentage and panicle grain count.

organicAlternatives.name: Well-cured Farmyard Manure (FYM)
organicAlternatives.benefits: Improves soil structure, water holding, and slow-releases balanced nutrients.

organicAlternatives.name: Vermicompost
organicAlternatives.benefits: Contains concentrated humus, active microbes, and plant growth regulators.

organicAlternatives.name: Biofertilizers (Azotobacter + PSB)
organicAlternatives.benefits: Biological nitrogen fixation and solubilization of fixed soil phosphorus.

fertilizerAdvisories.environmentalPrecautions: Never apply urea immediately before heavy rains to prevent nitrate runoff into local water bodies. Avoid excessive nitrogen to prevent pest outbreaks.
fertilizerAdvisories.referenceStandard: Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) Package of Practices

irrigationAdvisories.irrigationGuidance: Maintain adequate root-zone moisture during critical growth stages. For Wheat, prevent moisture stress during flowering and fruit/grain formation.

recommendedSchedule.timingOfDay: Early Morning (6 AM - 9 AM) or Evening

recommendedSchedule.interval: As per soil tension (when top 5cm is dry)

waterConservationTips: Adopt organic trash mulching to reduce soil surface evaporation by up to 35%.
Use alternate furrow irrigation in row crops to save 25% water without yield reduction.
Operate drip lines with pressure regulators to ensure uniform discharge across slopes.
waterStressIndicators: Wilting or drooping leaves during peak afternoon hours that fail to recover by evening.
Dull, grayish-green discoloration of vegetative foliage.
premature shedding of flowers and small immature pods/fruits.
irrigationAdvisories.overUnderPrecautions: Waterlogging causes root asphyxiation, accelerates Phytophthora and Fusarium root rot, and leaches valuable nitrates below root zone. Induces severe moisture stress, poor nutrient uptake, pollen sterility, and significant yield loss.

tasks.description: Summer deep ploughing to eradicate resting soil-borne pests, fungal spores, and perennial weed seeds.
Incorporate 5 tonnes FYM per acre. Treat certified seed with Trichoderma viride or recommended fungicide.
Sow at recommended line-to-line spacing. Place basal DAP and Potash 5cm below seed depth.
Crucial irrigation at Crown Root Initiation (CRI) / early tillering. Broadcast first dose of Neem Coated Urea.
Perform hand weeding or mechanical hoeing between rows to eliminate weed competition before canopy closure.
Provide second scheduled irrigation. Scout field for aphid colonies, leaf spots, and nutrient hunger signs.
Maintain soil moisture to support full grain plumpness. Avoid irrigation during strong windy days to prevent lodging.
Harvest when grains achieve golden maturity and moisture drops to 12-14%. Clean and bag under dry weather.
